meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

You asked for this meeting, Hale, so I'll let you start, but I have twenty minutes. Before anything else, I want to know who decided on that zero, and whether anyone heard from Owen before it went into the gradebook. He found out on his phone, in the middle of a class.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. And was Owen heard before you entered it, or after?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.

You didn't answer my question, Hale, and I'll come back to it. Turn the screen, I want to read that history myself, and I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, so where does that show up?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

Give me the page, I'll search it myself. Seventeen-year-olds get Shakespeare wrong, Hale, and you still haven't told me whether you spoke to Owen first. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Thursday at 8:15, in your room, before his class arrives, and nobody in that class hears a word about it. I want it in an email tonight, cc the principal, that the zero comes out of the gradebook now and nothing goes on file. If Owen sits it, it's to put this behind him, Hale, and for no other reason.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that Owen may complete a supervised rewrite in your room on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal supervising, and that if it holds up the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I still require written confirmation that the zero comes out of the gradebook now, that nothing is placed on file, that none of this is raised in front of his class, and a direct answer on whether Owen was heard before the zero was entered. I expect that email from you tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to the supervised rewrite Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal, while still wanting written confirmation that the zero comes out now, nothing goes on file, it stays quiet, and an answer on whether Owen was heard first.
What moved her: the version history with its exact times, because it was specific, dated, tied to his own work and something she could check; the line that is not in Hamlet pushed her further.
What cost ground: nothing cost a position, but sidestepping her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero kept her pressing and left an open item for her email.
Try next time: when she asked whether Owen was heard before you entered the mark, answer that plainly in one sentence before turning the screen to the version history.
